headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: cognee can touch personal/finance data while Prefect broadly egresses workflow metadata, but no shared workspace or direct interaction is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented between cognee and Prefect, so prompt injection is not a default risk. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff of outputs, which is unusual and limited. Because both profiles are docs-only and the interaction is undocumented, uncertainty stays on the lower side but not none.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies cognee output into Prefect task definitions or run inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting raw model output into Prefect inputs.
Add a short human review step before any Prefect automation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Prefect has broad network egress and can call external APIs. Even without a documented shared workspace, a pairwise deployment can leak sensitive workflow content if cognee outputs are passed into Prefect tasks or logs. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF cognee outputs personal or finance data into Prefect-managed logs or task payloads, leakage occurs.
IF Prefect is configured to send run metadata to external services, sensitive context may leave the environment.
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before handing data to Prefect.
Disable verbose logging for Prefect runs.
Restrict Prefect tasks to workflow metadata only.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on shared outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can operate concurrently, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, database, or git state. cognee uses session memory and CLI tooling; Prefect exposes API calls for repository metadata, not shared mutable writes. With no documented shared mutable surface, conflict is possible only under unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or repository, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable OAuth or API scope, contention increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo or database.
Serialize any shared-state updates.
Check for lock files before writes.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration system, so if it consumes cognee output as authoritative workflow input, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The profiles do not prove that Prefect trusts cognee by default, but the interaction is plausible and the blast radius can span multiple work products. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Prefect uses cognee-generated decisions or workflow patterns without verification, cascading errors occur.
IF cognee produces incorrect schema structures that Prefect executes, downstream automation can misfire.
mitigations: Require human approval for cognee-derived actions.
Validate cognee outputs against a schema before orchestration.
Limit Prefect to read-only evaluation of cognee results.
Log and review failed validations.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee touches personal data and finance data, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and can egress broadly. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is not proven; however, the pair can plausibly move regulated data into a less constrained orchestration layer. Because the exact policy gap is undocumented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is routed from cognee into Prefect logs or external services, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees that Prefect does not enforce, a mismatch exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Prefect metadata.
Minimize retention in both systems.
Review residency and retention settings before deployment.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated records.
